name: Connect onAir
goal: Help GMU IST students and faculty find useful opportunities through checked profiles, clear matches and reviewed posts.
pilot: First pilot: the GMU IST hub, with students, faculty, advisers, businesses and curators.
direction: Start with opportunity matching. Reuse one draft helper for profiles and posts. People check facts and approve posts.

processes.title: Profile preparation
processes.description: Read resume text, draft profile fields and ask about gaps. The member checks and edits the result.

processes.title: Opportunity discovery
processes.description: Rank posts by skills and interests. Explain each match and its gaps. Keep search and filters.

processes.title: Post drafting and review
processes.description: Draft posts from business source text. The business checks facts. A curator approves each hub post.

capabilities.title: Resume and listing intake
capabilities.description: Read common documents, text files and spreadsheets. Use PatriotAI for pictures and scanned PDFs, then check and edit the extracted text. Files can be up to 10 MB; AI reads up to 10 pages.

capabilities.title: Rules-based matching
capabilities.description: Scores use required skills (70%), preferred skills (20%) and interests (10%). Empty groups share their weight. Scores show skill coverage, not the chance of a job offer.

capabilities.title: Review and backup
capabilities.description: Save review records in this browser. Export or restore a JSON backup. This does not create a shared account or publish to WordPress.

capabilities.title: PatriotAI profile drafts
capabilities.description: Generate a draft in this website through the PatriotAI model API. Source references create exact quotes. Unsupported fields stay blank with a warning; valid fields remain available for review.

capabilities.title: Agent reads the demo catalog
capabilities.description: An agent tool fetched six fictional listings. It also reproduced the rules scores. This does not prove that AI makes better matches.

capabilities.title: AI ranking and hub connection
capabilities.description: Profile drafting uses AI. Opportunity scores still use rules. AI ranking, full WordPress fields and approved hub posting remain to be built and tested.

approach.title: Parser
approach.description: Read file text and explicit fields. Keep this step even if AI handles the next step.

approach.title: AI
approach.description: Test whether AI helps when a profile and a post use different words. Check facts, match reasons and missing skills.

approach.title: Compare both
approach.description: Test AI and rules on the same labeled data. Compare match quality, missed results, speed and cost. Keep rules or a hybrid if AI adds too little value.

architecture.title: Browser and parser
architecture.description: Read text, edit fields, show match reasons and collect reviews.

architecture.title: Drafting server
architecture.description: Check source text and model replies. Keep the service key on the server, outside the public site. The demo does not require a login.

architecture.title: PatriotAI model API
architecture.description: GPT-4o drafts profile fields from text. A live test passed on November 17. Confirm real-data use and long-term ownership before a pilot.

architecture.title: WordPress and reviewers
architecture.description: Read full records and ACF fields. Use the hub’s categories. Keep posting rights with approved people.

patriot.testedDirection: PatriotAI agent → public fictional catalog: tested read-only GET.
patriot.pendingDirection: Website → drafting server → PatriotAI GPT-4o model: connected for profile drafts. This calls the model API, not the saved personal agent.
patriot.access: The capstone demo needs no owner login. The API key stays on the server. Drafting sends only the source text you choose; model replies still need review.
patriot.request: Before real use, confirm allowed data, consent, API ownership, key rotation, support and budget with Mason ITS and the sponsor. Live profile drafting does not prove match quality or WordPress integration.

curation: Start with student, team, faculty and adviser profiles, plus research and capstone posts. Agree on the first content set and its sources.
Members check their profiles. Businesses and curators check posts. Keep source records and corrections. Leave unknown facts blank.
Later, scan approved sources for internships, jobs, scholarships, research and events. Remove repeats and check links. Send drafts to a curator. This scan is not built yet.

pilotTargets.target: At least 95% of agreed required fields across 10 profiles; no invented critical facts
pilotTargets.validation: Compare fields against source material and log member corrections.

pilotTargets.target: At least 90% accuracy on agreed reviewer labels
pilotTargets.validation: Use 10 profiles and 40 opportunities with an agreed taxonomy and scoring method.

pilotTargets.target: At least 7 relevant results in 8 of 10 Top-10 lists
pilotTargets.validation: Retain reviewer judgments and compare AI, hybrid and rules on the same data.
Measure on the agreed host, load and complete-record retrieval path.

pilotTargets.target: Median profile review within 5 minutes; post review within 10 minutes; zero unauthorized publication
pilotTargets.validation: Time 10 profile and 10 post reviews; test roles and approval records.

pilotTargets.target: Sponsor-agreed budget and improvement against a successful-task baseline
pilotTargets.validation: Measure completed tasks, corrections, hosting allocation, support effort and incremental AI use.

baseline: Earlier checks saw one failed login and one failed search. We still need times for completed tasks, post review and pilot costs. These targets need sponsor agreement; they are not results we have achieved.

decisions.question: What must the first pilot deliver?
decisions.detail: Agree on matching first, the needed profile and post tools, pilot users, content, limits and who signs off.

decisions.question: How do we read full hub records?
decisions.detail: Confirm the test site, WordPress API, ACF fields, categories and access. Review which parts of Sai’s matching work we can reuse.

decisions.question: Who will own the AI connection for the pilot?
decisions.owner: Mason ITS and onAir technical mentors
decisions.detail: The demo calls the PatriotAI model API. Confirm allowed data, hosting, key rotation, limits and the long-term service owner.

decisions.question: What data may leave the hub?
decisions.detail: Agree on consent, allowed data, storage time and access before using real records. Mason’s FAQ describes outside search and some outside model calls.

decisions.question: Who reviews and publishes?
decisions.detail: Name who checks facts, fixes errors and approves posts. Agree on posting rights and review records.

decisions.question: How will we judge match quality?
decisions.detail: Agree on labels, test data, task times, speed and budget. Set a clear test for when AI beats the rules.

decisions.question: Who keeps the system running?
decisions.detail: Name the owner for hosting, checks, backup, restore, guides and training. Agree on who handles faults.

roadmap.deliverable: Marcus and Jayce confirm scope, approved access, field routes and labeled data. Confirm winter-break work capacity.
Khizer and Zain finish editable fields, source checks and reviewed drafts.
Anthony and Marcus build ranking and reasons, then compare AI with rules on ten profiles and forty listings.
Mahnoor and Jayce build source-backed drafts and test business and curator approval. This work runs alongside matching.
The whole team tests connected hub flows, failed calls, permissions and recovery.
Anthony and the team close defects and seek sponsor acceptance against the agreed pilot targets.
Zain and the team release the product and complete training, operating guides and recovery handoff. March 5 is the planning target for an early March final product, pending the exact course cutoff.
